root_cause.text: `ionic_create_cq()` in the RDMA/ionic control path allocated `struct ionic_cq_resp resp` on the stack without zero-initializing it, and only partially filled `cqid[]` based on `udma_mask`, leaving the reserved bytes and sometimes `cqid[1]` uninitialized and copied back to userspace.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `struct ionic_cq_resp resp;` to `struct ionic_cq_resp resp = {};`, and the CVE text states `rsvd[7]` was “NEVER SET <- LEAK” while `cqid[1]` could also remain unwritten when `udma_mask` only had bit 0 set, causing up to 11 bytes of kernel stack data to leak.

intent_record.intent_summary: Zero-initialize the CQ response structure to prevent use of uninitialized stack contents during CQ creation.
intent_record.what: In `ionic_create_cq()`, the local variable `resp` of type `struct ionic_cq_resp` was changed from an uninitialized declaration to a zero-initialized declaration (`struct ionic_cq_resp resp = {};`).
intent_record.how: This ensures the completion queue response structure starts with all fields set to zero before it is used, preventing any later code from observing or copying indeterminate stack data if only part of the structure is populated.

grouping_result.intent: Zero-initialize the CQ response structure to prevent use of uninitialized stack contents during CQ creation.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it zero-initializes the CQ response structure in ionic_create_cq() to avoid leaking uninitialized stack data back to userspace.

candidates.rationale: This stack-allocated response structure was not zero-initialized before being partially populated, so uninitialized bytes could be copied back to userspace.

vuln_statements.explanation: This stack-allocated response object was not zero-initialized before being partially populated, allowing reserved bytes and possibly cqid[1] to remain uninitialized and later be copied to userspace.

bic_trace_step.reason: YES, the function body is enough to determine the issue because it shows the allocation, population, and copy-out of the response struct. The vulnerable construct is present: `struct ionic_cq_resp resp;` is declared on the stack at line 1221 without initialization, and later only `resp.udma_mask = vcq->udma_mask;` is set before `ib_copy_to_udata(udata, &resp, sizeof(resp));` at lines 1261-1264. The loop only fills `resp.cqid[udma_idx]` for indices that pass `vcq->udma_mask`, so any reserved bytes and any unfilled `cqid[]` elements remain uninitialized and are copied to userspace. There is no zeroing such as `memset(&resp, 0, sizeof(resp))`, so the fix is not present in this version.
